exposure: Urine soluble triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells (sTREM-1) levels
cohort: The cohort consisted of 62 preterm neonates evaluated for late-onset sepsis, with 31 having culture-proven sepsis and 31 suspected of having sepsis.
finding: Preterm neonates with culture-proven late-onset sepsis had significantly higher urine sTREM-1 levels compared to those with suspected sepsis, and urine sTREM-1 at a cut-off of 78.5 pg/mL showed good sensitivity (0.90) and specificity (0.78) for detecting sepsis.
mod_finding: There were no significant differences in delivery mode between the culture-proven sepsis group and the suspected sepsis group.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken synchronously at the time preterm neonates were evaluated for late-onset sepsis.
birth_weight: N/A (not specified, only mentioned as having no significant difference between groups)
